text: The failover group from Lesson 11 has never actually been triggered. This lesson finally runs the drill -- and claims-processing immediately starts throwing write errors.
The instinct is to panic and fail straight back. Instead, we verify one layer at a time: first, did Azure's side of the failover actually work?
Checking the failover group's status confirms thornridge-sql-server-secondary correctly promoted to Primary. The orchestration layer did exactly what it was built to do.
A direct write against the new primary succeeds immediately. The database itself is healthy and fully writable -- which rules out a database-layer problem entirely.
Two layers are now proven healthy. The failure has to be in the one place neither check touched: how the application itself decides where to connect.
